claims.wording: Disk Map is made by Vikom Media in Vancouver, Canada.
claims.excerpt: Disk Map is made by Vikom Media in Vancouver, Canada.

claims.wording: The direct download is advertised as version 1.4 (8 MB), for macOS 15 Sequoia or later on Apple silicon and Intel.
claims.excerpt: Free. Version 1.4 (8 MB). macOS 15 Sequoia or later, Apple silicon and Intel.
claims.conditions: Not a checksum, binary size measurement, signing check, or successful installation; not proof of App Store availability.

claims.wording: Disk Map is advertised as free, with no ads, trial or account.
claims.excerpt: Is it free? Yes. No ads, trial or account.
claims.conditions: Current direct-site offer, no recurring amount advertised. Terms reserve future charges disclosed before payment; not a perpetual free-price guarantee. App Store offer not independently verified.

claims.wording: The licence grants object-code use on Macs owned or controlled by the user, for personal or internal business purposes; it is not an open-source grant.
claims.excerpt: a personal, non-exclusive, non-transferable, non-sublicensable, revocable licence to download, install and use the App, in object code form only

claims.wording: Disk Map documents a disk/folder treemap above a table of the same folders.
claims.excerpt: It scans a disk or folder and draws it as a treemap, where every folder is a tile sized by the space it takes, above a table of the same folders.

claims.wording: Space Advisor selects steps toward a space goal for review before Apply Selected; personal files are not preselected.
claims.excerpt: Change anything, then press Apply Selected. | Your own files are never ticked for you.
claims.conditions: Do not repeat safe/lossless marketing as a tested guarantee. Read D10 for irreversible actions.

claims.wording: Documented suggestions include online-only cloud files, duplicate-to-APFS-clone merging, caches, installers and build output; project grouping is documented.
claims.excerpt: Cloud files kept online only, duplicates merged so they stop taking the space twice | Caches, installers for apps you already have, build output. | Build output and dependencies, grouped by project
claims.locator: Space Advisor and A closer look
claims.conditions: No runtime validation, supported-cache catalogue or cloud-plan costs established.

claims.wording: Disk Map documents previous-scan changes, live updates, free-space menu-bar display and opt-in disk warnings.
claims.excerpt: Each scan is compared with the last | Folders grow as the scan runs, then keep up as files change. | Only if you allow them | from the last 20 scans
claims.locator: Changes, Live, Menu bar, Questions; privacy section 1
claims.conditions: Do not claim no monitoring or no recurring-growth support. Process/helper CPU and RAM grouping is separately not verified.

claims.wording: Disk Map documents a Space Freed by Deleting estimate that accounts for shared APFS data.
claims.excerpt: APFS copies share data. See both the space a folder takes and what deleting it frees. | Sizes and other figures shown by the App are estimates
claims.locator: Space Freed by Deleting; terms section 5
claims.conditions: Not independently verified accuracy or guaranteed recovered bytes.

claims.wording: Not every cleanup action is reversible: the terms describe emptying Trash and requesting deletion of local Time Machine snapshots, and require review and backups.
claims.excerpt: The App can move files and folders to the Trash, empty the Trash, and ask macOS to delete local Time Machine snapshots. Some of these actions can’t be undone.
claims.conditions: Qualifies homepage reassurance that items moved to Trash can be restored. Rebuilds can take time/cost or fail.

claims.wording: The policy says scan history stays local, while choosing Ask AI sends a folder report to the selected agent, which may send it to its own service.
claims.excerpt: folder and file names, sizes, dates, space by kind of file, what changed and what the App suggests, but never what’s inside your files | The agent may send the report to its own service, under that service’s privacy policy.
claims.locator: Privacy section 1, Asking an AI agent
claims.conditions: Vendor statement, not a network audit. Never claim all workflows are offline or nothing ever leaves the Mac. External AI requirements/prices not verified.

claims.wording: The direct version works without Full Disk Access, skipping protected folders; its daily Sparkle update checks can be disabled.
claims.excerpt: Without it, protected folders like Mail and Messages are skipped and marked with a lock. | You can turn automatic checks off in the App’s Settings.
claims.conditions: Mac App Store sandbox behavior is described in policy, not proof of a live store listing. No installation, signing/notarization or runtime prerequisites independently checked.

claims.wording: Grouped app/helper CPU and memory monitoring, unattended exact-approval scheduled cleanup and exact tool-cache adapter coverage: not verified for Disk Map.
claims.excerpt: Sources describe disk history, project build output and menu-bar free space; do not establish these additional dimensions.

claims.wording: Breathing Room is a free Apache-2.0 Mac maintenance preview; optional AI Care is advertised at $5 USD/month or $50 USD/year.
claims.excerpt: AI Care is advertised at $5 USD/month or $50 USD/year | macOS 13+ | Python 3.10+ | Apple Development signed, not Developer ID signed or notarized
claims.conditions: 0.1.0-preview.1; no clean-machine/physical-Intel runtime validation. Hosted AI requires internet/authentication; free local core distinct from paid advertised care. Renewal and applicable checkout taxes; enforcement/AI allowance unknown.

claims.wording: Breathing Room source implements storage views, grouped app/helper CPU and memory, developer cleanup discovery, local activity history and exact-approval daily care while running.
claims.excerpt: Source implementation is not proof that every feature works in the distributed installer. | Scheduled care: ... only remembered exact approvals are eligible.
claims.conditions: Not hands-on competitor testing or binary parity verification. Optional automatic verified Ruff-cache mode is an explicit exception to per-action asking. Hosted questions/history/tool outputs can leave Mac.

workflow.title: Plan Mac storage cleanup without trusting folder size alone
workflow.primaryIntent: Understand size versus reclaim estimates before selecting a target-based cleanup plan
workflow.track: how-to-guide; documented workflow, not tested tutorial
workflow.audience: Mac owners with a storage target, especially project and cloud-file users
outline: A large tile is an investigation lead, not deletion permission
Use Disk Map's treemap and Space Freed by Deleting estimate together
Review Advisor's proposed cloud, clone, rebuildable and personal-file steps
Check previous-scan growth rather than deleting the largest folder repeatedly
Choose broader app/process investigation only when that is the actual job
workflow.informationGain: A decision checklist separating file size, vendor reclaim estimate, cloud re-download/rebuild costs and irreversible actions; no benchmark numbers.
workflow.interactionPass: Plan a static decision aid: identify ownership → check backup and rebuild/download cost → distinguish estimate from actual free space → review exact selected action. No cleanup execution or forced code demo.
workflow.visualPlan: Official Disk Map app UI directly after lead only after clearance; current-source Breathing Room Space preview later with required example-data caption.
questions: Why can folder size differ from space freed?
Which suggested actions need a backup or rebuild plan?
Do I need storage history or app/process investigation?
workflow.keywordStatus: Editorial intent hypotheses, no search-volume or SERP claims
workflow.boundary: General APFS explanations need Apple primary documentation before extending beyond attributed Disk Map documentation; no fabricated FAQ/statistics or hands-on claims.
